vocab.definition: a huge lattice of atoms joined by covalent bonds.
carbon, each atom bonded to 4 others — very hard.
carbon in layers, each atom bonded to 3 — conducts.

misconceptions.right: They have very high melting points (strong bonds).
Diamond has no free electrons, so it doesn't conduct.

misconceptions.wrong: Graphite's layers are held by strong bonds.
misconceptions.right: Layers are held by weak forces, so they slide.

questions.text: Explain why giant covalent structures have very high melting points. [2 marks]
Explain why diamond is so hard. [2 marks]
Explain why graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not. [3 marks]
Explain why graphite is soft and slippery. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: In graphite each carbon bonds to ______ others, leaving one ______ electron to carry charge.

questions.text: Suggest a use for diamond and a use for graphite, linked to their properties. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Many strong covalent bonds = lots of energy to melt = very high melting point.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does graphite's free electron make it useful as an electrode?
